s1.syndrome_frame: Subacute onset of painful swelling and muscle weakness with systemic inflammation and multi-organ involvement
salient_findings: Painful swelling of the calves
Elevated LDH and CK
Diffuse subcutaneous edema on CT scan
Muscle biopsy showing interstitial and perivascular T-cell and macrophage infiltrates
Cardiac involvement with myocarditis and atrial fibrillation
Neurologic involvement with myelitis
key_facts: 57-year-old man with stage cS4a mantle cell lymphoma in complete remission
Presented with painful swelling of the calves in August 2018
No evidence of deep venous thrombosis or soft-tissue infection
Brief gastroenteritis episode at the time of presentation
Diuretics gave transient relief
Systemic steroids and discontinuation of ibrutinib had no effect
Elevated LDH and CK on laboratory tests
Negative autoimmune serology
CT scan showed no lymphoma relapse but diffuse subcutaneous edema
ECOG performance status 3 at the time of hospitalization
Muscle biopsy demonstrated interstitial and perivascular T-cell and macrophage infiltrates
Developed acute kidney injury secondary to rhabdomyolysis
Cardiac MRI confirmed myocarditis
Spinal MRI demonstrated a hyperintense lesion concerning for myelitis
CSF analysis showed leukocyte count 329/μl, lactate 3.5 mmol/L, and protein 79.6 mg/dl

shortlist.label: Polymyositis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated CK, muscle biopsy demonstrated interstitial and perivascular T-cell and macrophage infiltrates

shortlist.label: Dermatomyositis
shortlist.why_kept: Painful swelling and muscle weakness with systemic inflammation

shortlist.label: Necrotizing autoimmune myopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated CK, muscle biopsy demonstrated necrosis and regeneration

shortlist.label: Ibrutinib-induced myositis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient was taking ibrutinib, which is a known cause of myositis

shortlist.label: Rhabdomyolysis
shortlist.why_kept: Developed acute kidney injury secondary to rhabdomyolysis

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with painful swelling of the calves, elevated CK and LDH, and muscle biopsy demonstrating interstitial and perivascular T-cell and macrophage infiltrates, necrosis, and regeneration are consistent with necrotizing autoimmune myopathy. The lack of skin manifestations rules out dermatomyositis, and the absence of a clear association with ibrutinib discontinuation makes ibrutinib-induced myositis less likely.

rejected.label: Polymyositis
rejected.why: Lack of specific muscle biopsy findings and presence of necrosis and regeneration, which are more characteristic of necrotizing autoimmune myopathy

rejected.label: Ibrutinib-induced myositis
rejected.why: Discontinuation of ibrutinib did not lead to improvement

rejected.label: Rhabdomyolysis
rejected.why: While the patient developed rhabdomyolysis, it is a complication of the underlying myopathy rather than the primary diagnosis
